   1: # CHANGELOG — cubesat-cl-ids (CubeSat TinyML CIL)
   2: 
   3: All protocol/method changes are logged here with **why** (journal-review rationale).
   4: Target story is unchanged: **onboard class-incremental IDS under memory + uplink budgets (simulation-only).**
   5: No generic IDS datasets are added — CuCD-ID stays primary, STIN stays stress-test.
   6: 
   7: ## [2026-10-23] v6.2 packaging + claim reframing (no experiment rerun)
   8: - **Artifact identity:** package version/report set to **v6.2**
   9:   (`v6_2_project_report_final.md`); manifest and README/PROJECT_CONTEXT links
  10:   aligned. Historical v5.x entries are retained as history.
  11: - **Packaging cleanup:** removed the empty brace-expansion directory
  12:   `{src,experiments,tests,data` and all `__pycache__` directories.
  13: - **Frozen-hparam hardening:** `load_frozen_hparams_strict()` now validates
  14:   every architecture × method entry, non-empty `hparams`, and `lr`/`epochs`;
  15:   added `tests/test_frozen_hparams.py`. No config values changed.
  16: - **Claim reframing:** report and README now present a resource-aware benchmark
  17:   and negative-result study, not a claim that `full` wins. Added explicit
  18:   boundaries for `full` vs replay, temporal-purged collapse, feature-order
  19:   power (one split, two seeds), task-order budget-mode identity by
  20:   construction, CuCD-ID-only tuning with STIN transfer, tuning/confirmatory
  21:   seed overlap, and the λ=0 control. No CSV/JSON result values changed.
  22: 
  23: ## [2026-10-22] v6 confirmatory validity rerun (810 runs, 15 seeds)
  24: - **Calibration/selection split fixed:** validation is now 20% of each
  25:   per-class pool, then split 50/50 into disjoint halves. BiC/Fisher fit on
  26:   the calibration half; hyperparameter and model selection score only on the
  27:   selection half. The split seed uses stable class identity rather than
  28:   `task_id`, so task-order permutations cannot silently change which rows are
  29:   used for calibration. Added `tests/test_calib_split.py` and extended
  30:   `tests/test_task_order.py`.
  31: - **Seed count:** main matrix increased from 10 to 15 seeds (810 runs). With
  32:   216 all-pairwise comparisons per metric, n=10 could not reach Holm
  33:   significance; n=15 gives an exact-test floor of `6.1e-5`, so the full
  34:   family can be corrected honestly.
  35: - **Statistics:** fixed 216-comparison family per metric (all unordered
  36:   method pairs within dataset x architecture), Holm across the full family.
  37:   Current results: 162/216 ACC and 164/216 Macro-F1 significant. Added
  38:   matched-replay and EWC-lambda controls (450 runs); 7/30 control
  39:   comparisons survive Holm. All tests are pre-specified and exploratory.
  40: - **Few-shot:** 420 runs; both `fixed` (150 calib + 150 select per class) and
  41:   `scaled` (K calib + K select per class) protocols. Calibration payload is
  42:   charged only to BiC/EWC/full; selection payload is never charged.
  43: - **Task order:** 144 runs split into two-class-T0-first primary permutations
  44:   and single-class-first degenerate (no-op first update) permutations. Primary
  45:   per-order mean spread is 0.0146.
  46: - **Feature order:** BiC-corrected permutations now include
  47:   `X_calib`/`X_select`; 96 runs.
  48: - **Memory:** retained-update state is the cumulative calibration half;
  49:   selection arrays are excluded. Largest persistent state 18.53 KB; largest
  50:   host-estimated peak update RAM 348.34 KB.
  51: - **Parallel execution:** all heavy scripts run four fork-based workers with
  52:   one BLAS thread each (`CL_JOBS=4`). Full confirmatory run: 3h59m compute,
  53:   4h07m wall including restart. Fixed a missing `time` import in
  54:   `experiments/run_ablation.py` that stopped the first orchestration pass;
  55:   the remaining stages were resumed successfully.
  56: - **Artifacts regenerated:** 810 main runs, 756 tuning rows (2268 seed-runs),
  57:   420 few-shot, 270 temporal, 225 leakage, 1,890 per-class, 450 controls,
  58:   216+216 stats, 21 figures, manifest, `RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`, and
  59:   `v5_4_project_report_final.md`.
  60: - **Why:** the previous run shared one validation pool for calibration and
  61:   selection, could not support Holm correction over the full 216-comparison
  62:   family at 10 seeds, and did not report both few-shot calibration protocols.
  63:   These were validity issues, not presentation issues.
  64: 
  65: ## [2026-10-21] v5.4 Q2/Q3 correctness + provenance hardening (results rerun)
  66: - **Temporal ordering:** `src/data_utils.py` now orders by unwrapped circular
  67:   `TimeRadians`; the 0.02 rad purge remains a documented proxy. The old raw
  68:   sort broke at the 0→2π wrap.
  69: - **EWC:** Fisher is estimated from a class-balanced cumulative old+new
  70:   validation pool instead of current-task data only; `train.py`/`cmmu.py`
  71:   docstrings corrected.
  72: - **Leakage:** new `experiments/run_leakage_ablation.py` retrains CuCD-ID/MLP
  73:   after removing time/CCSDS-ID/20-s-window feature groups (5 variants × 3
  74:   methods × 10 seeds). README/report now disclose that the IID split can share
  75:   overlapping windows and is a benchmark estimand, not a deployment estimate.
  76: - **Tuning:** all 9 methods (including `joint`/`joint_scratch`) and all
  77:   architectures now tune on validation with `epochs` and EWC `gamma`
  78:   dimensions; one training pass per combo. Grid sizes capped for runtime.
  79: - **Stats:** ACC and Macro-F1 exact paired permutation files; STIN headline
  80:   comparisons added; Holm applied within each metric.
  81: - **Reporting:** `generate_summary_report.py` now emits both
  82:   `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` and the auto-generated
  83:   `v5_4_project_report_final.md`, with a computed executive summary. All
  84:   result values come from CSV/JSON; stale hand-typed result tables were
  85:   removed from README/PAPER_PLAN/SUPERVISOR_SUMMARY.
  86: - **Consistency:** `check_consistency.py` accepts all 9 tuned methods and
  87:   writes `results/consistency_check.json`; `create_manifest.py` reads that
  88:   status dynamically and now also hashes the v5.4 report.
  89: - **Ablations/robustness:** `run_ablation.py` now uses `val_frac=0.10`;
  90:   `run_robustness.py` uses the strict frozen-hparams loader.
  91: - **Provenance:** citations and simulated-telemetry scope added to README,
  92:   PROJECT_CONTEXT, PAPER_PLAN, and the final report; per-class figure ylabel
  93:   corrected; few-shot Pareto now plots uplink KB vs Macro-F1; leakage figure
  94:   added.
  95: - **Why:** a reviewer can otherwise mistake simulated, overlapping-window IID
  96:   results for deployment evidence, and current-task-only Fisher plus raw
  97:   circular-time sorting are correctness defects.

 237: - `run_arch_tune.py`: quarantined as exploratory — selection now on validation `V` (was test `R`), base configs from frozen file, not in `run_all.py`, report §7.2 labeled as such.

 240: ### H-2 Bounded herding + teacher accounting + performed compute
 241: - `src/train.py`: BiC/iCaRL herding rebuild selects from resident buffer + incoming batch only (unbounded `herding_data` history removed); returns last frozen `teacher` plus performed counters (`train_steps_total`, `train_samples_total`, `teacher_samples_total`).
 242: - `run_main.py`: peak RAM uses per-step replay minibatch (not full buffer) and the real teacher object; `macs_per_update` from performed student/teacher samples (not union-size estimate).

 269: ## [2026-09-20] Q2-Submission Hardening — 8 Critical Fixes (COMPLETED, results regenerated)
 270: 
 271: ### Q2-1 `src/train.py` — BiC stage-local correction bug fix
 272: - **Fixed:** `BiasCorrector.apply()` now only corrects `n_old:n_old+n_new` (previously corrected all future classes).
 273: - **Fixed:** `fit_stage()` now stores `n_new` per stage; stage dict = `{"n_old", "n_new", "alpha", "beta"}`.
 274: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.3 — baseline with incorrect implementation is unpublishable. All BiC results regenerated.
 275: 
 276: ### Q2-2 `experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py` / `src/train.py` — Train/Val/Test methodology
 277: - Sweep now uses `val_frac=0.10` on STIN; hyperparameters selected on **validation ACC_val - FM_val**, never test.
 278: - `train_continual()` returns validation matrix `V` alongside test matrix `R`.
 279: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.1 — test-set leakage invalidates main comparison if uncorrected.
 280: 
 281: ### Q2-3 `experiments/run_validation_tune.py` (NEW) — Per-method/arch validation tuning
 282: - 7 methods × 3 architectures tuned on CuCD-ID validation (3 seeds each), small grids per method family.
 283: - Winners frozen to `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` → used by ALL subsequent experiments.
 284: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.2 — single sweep on MLP/STIN does not transfer to GRU/CNN (confirmed by ablation).
 285: 
 286: ### Q2-4 `src/data_utils.py` / `experiments/run_purged_temporal.py` (NEW) — Purged temporal protocol
 287: - Added `build_cucd_id_tasks_purged_temporal()` with 22s-equivalent (0.02 rad) purge gaps on `TimeRadians`.
 288: - Layout: `[Train | Purge | Val | Purge | Test]` — exceeds 20s sliding-window horizon + 20-22s clearing pauses.
 289: - STIN keeps existing `id`-based temporal (no purge — secondary stress test only).
 290: - Dual-protocol evaluation: **IID (benchmark)** + **Forward Temporal + Purge (stress test)**.
 291: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.6/0.7 — IID numbers (~0.92) vs temporal (~0.20) gap must be explicit, not hidden.
 292: 
 293: ### Q2-5 `src/metrics.py` / `src/train.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` — Dual memory + compute accounting
 294: - **Persistent footprint:** INT8 weights + INT8 replay + FP16 EWC (deployed storage).
 295: - **Peak training RAM:** FP32 weights + gradients + Adam(2×params) + activations + batch + replay_batch + teacher + temp.
 296: - **MAC/update:** MAC/sample × N_train_samples × epochs (not just MAC/forward).
 297: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.14/15/18 — Q2 systems reviewer will demand complete resource accounting.
 298: 
 299: ### Q2-6 `experiments/config.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` / `experiments/run_fewshot.py` — Final consistent rerun
 300: - **Main matrix:** 10 seeds (540 runs: 2 datasets × 3 archs × 9 methods × 10 seeds) with frozen per-method/arch hparams.
 301: - **Few-shot:** 5 seeds, inherits frozen hparams, only K varies (K=5..300), uplink Pareto outputs.
 302: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.4/9/10 — central comparison must be internally consistent and statistically defensible.
 303: 
 304: ### Q2-7 `src/metrics.py` / `experiments/run_stats.py` / `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py` — Journal-grade metrics + stats
 305: - **Primary metrics:** Macro-F1, Balanced Accuracy, BWT/FM (Accuracy supplementary).
 306: - **Per-class:** Final F1 + forgetting for each attack class (CuCD-ID).
 307: - **Stats:** Exact paired permutation test (SciPy if available, else NumPy) + Holm correction + Cohen's d + 95% CI.
 308: - Headline comparisons only (no elaborate stats for every ablation).
 309: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.10/11/23/24 — "p=0.043 proves superiority" is not Q2-citable.
 310: 
 311: ### Q2-8 `experiments/run_feature_order.py` (NEW) — Architecture interpretation fix
 312: - 4 feature permutations × MLP/GRU/CNN × 4 methods × 2 seeds.
 313: - MLP stable; GRU/CNN sensitive → confirms MLP as primary tabular backbone, GRU/CNN as stress tests.
 314: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.21/22 — GRU/CNN on reshaped tabular features are not genuine temporal models.
 315: 
 316: ### Q2-9 New tooling for reproducibility
 317: - `experiments/check_consistency.py` — Verifies main vs few-shot hyperparameter consistency, seed counts, config provenance.
 318: - `experiments/create_manifest.py` — Creates `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` with full provenance (git commit, env, datasets, protocols, frozen hparams, outputs).
 319: - `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` — Complete machine-readable reproducibility record.
 320: 
 321: ### Pipeline integration
 322: - `run_all.py`: CORE (gradient → sweep → validation_tune → main) → PHASE2 (purged_temporal → fewshot → feature_order → ablations → per_class → stats → robustness) → REPORT (plots → summary).
 323: - `analysis/plots.py`: CI bars, Pareto figures, dual-protocol comparison, updated column names for persistent/peak memory.
 324: - `experiments/generate_summary_report.py`: Journal tables (Macro-F1 primary), dual memory, uplink Pareto.

 336: - Sweep now uses `val_frac=0.10` on STIN; hyperparameters selected on **validation ACC_val - FM_val**, never test.
 337: - `train_continual()` returns validation matrix `V` alongside test matrix `R`.
 338: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.1 — test-set leakage invalidates main comparison if uncorrected.
 339: 
 340: ### Q2-3 `experiments/run_validation_tune.py` (NEW) — Per-method/arch validation tuning
 341: - 7 methods × 3 architectures tuned on CuCD-ID validation (3 seeds each), small grids per method family.
 342: - Winners frozen to `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` → used by ALL subsequent experiments.
 343: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.2 — single sweep on MLP/STIN does not transfer to GRU/CNN (confirmed by ablation).
 344: 
 345: ### Q2-4 `src/data_utils.py` / `experiments/run_purged_temporal.py` (NEW) — Purged temporal protocol
 346: - Added `build_cucd_id_tasks_purged_temporal()` with 22s-equivalent (0.02 rad) purge gaps on `TimeRadians`.
 347: - Layout: `[Train | Purge | Val | Purge | Test]` — exceeds 20s sliding-window horizon + 20-22s clearing pauses.
 348: - STIN keeps existing `id`-based temporal (no purge — secondary stress test only).
 349: - Dual-protocol evaluation: **IID (benchmark)** + **Forward Temporal + Purge (stress test)**.
 350: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.6/0.7 — IID numbers (~0.92) vs temporal (~0.20) gap must be explicit, not hidden.
 351: 
 352: ### Q2-5 `src/metrics.py` / `src/train.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` — Dual memory + compute accounting
 353: - **Persistent footprint:** INT8 weights + INT8 replay + FP16 EWC (deployed storage).
 354: - **Peak training RAM:** FP32 weights + gradients + Adam(2×params) + activations + batch + replay_batch + teacher + temp.
 355: - **MAC/update:** MAC/sample × N_train_samples × epochs (not just MAC/forward).
 356: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.14/15/18 — Q2 systems reviewer will demand complete resource accounting.
 357: 
 358: ### Q2-6 `experiments/config.py` / `experiments/run_main.py` / `experiments/run_fewshot.py` — Final consistent rerun
 359: - **Main matrix:** 10 seeds (540 runs: 2 datasets × 3 archs × 9 methods × 10 seeds) with frozen per-method/arch hparams.
 360: - **Few-shot:** 5 seeds, inherits frozen hparams, only K varies (K=5..300), uplink Pareto outputs.
 361: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.4/9/10 — central comparison must be internally consistent and statistically defensible.
 362: 
 363: ### Q2-7 `src/metrics.py` / `experiments/run_stats.py` / `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py` — Journal-grade metrics + stats
 364: - **Primary metrics:** Macro-F1, Balanced Accuracy, BWT/FM (Accuracy supplementary).
 365: - **Per-class:** Final F1 + forgetting for each attack class (CuCD-ID).
 366: - **Stats:** Exact paired permutation test (SciPy if available, else NumPy) + Holm correction + Cohen's d + 95% CI.
 367: - Headline comparisons only (no elaborate stats for every ablation).
 368: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.10/11/23/24 — "p=0.043 proves superiority" is not Q2-citable.
 369: 
 370: ### Q2-8 `experiments/run_feature_order.py` (NEW) — Architecture interpretation fix
 371: - 4 feature permutations × MLP/GRU/CNN × 4 methods × 2 seeds.
 372: - MLP stable; GRU/CNN sensitive → confirms MLP as primary tabular backbone, GRU/CNN as stress tests.
 373: - **Why:** Reviewer P0.21/22 — GRU/CNN on reshaped tabular features are not genuine temporal models.
 374: 
 375: ### Pipeline integration
 376: - `run_all.py`: CORE (gradient → sweep → validation_tune → main) → PHASE2 (purged_temporal → fewshot → feature_order → ablations → per_class → stats → robustness) → REPORT (plots → summary).
 377: - `analysis/plots.py`: CI bars, Pareto figures, dual-protocol comparison, updated column names for persistent/peak memory.
 378: - `experiments/generate_summary_report.py`: Journal tables (Macro-F1 primary), dual memory, uplink Pareto.

 380: ## [Unreleased] Phase 0 — MUST-FIX protocol corrections (no results invalidated, old API kept)
 381: 
 382: ### 0.1 `src/data_utils.py` — train/val/test + temporal (leakage-safe) splits
 383: - **Added:** `Task.X_val / y_val` (optional, default `None`), `TaskSequence.split_mode`, `val_frac` plumbing.
 384: - **Added:** `_stratified_train_val_test_split()` — test is locked before any train/val sampling; val is carved from train pool only.
 385: - **Added:** `build_cucd_id_tasks_temporal()` / `build_stin_tasks_temporal()` — per-class **block (time-ordered) split** instead of row-shuffle, because CuCD-ID features contain `SlidingWindow* / MessageCountInWindow / MessageRateInWindow` computed over neighbouring rows; random row-shuffle leaks correlated windows between train and test and inflates absolute ACC. Old builders kept byte-identical behaviour when `val_frac=0.0` and `split_mode="random"`.
 386: - **Why:** reviewer P0.1 (sliding-window leakage) + P0.2 (no val/test separation). Relative rankings (replay >> finetune) survive leakage, but absolute numbers (e.g. MLP 0.93 / permuted-order 0.995) are not Q1/Q2-credible without this.
 387: 
 388: ### 0.2 `src/train.py` — true joint-from-scratch + bias-correction hook + balanced replay option
 389: - **Added:** `method="joint_scratch"` — re-initialises the model and trains on the union of all training data seen so far at each task boundary. Old `method="joint"` is kept but renamed in docs as `cumulative warm-start` (it continues from current weights, `train.py` pool logic). New method is the strict upper bound.
 390: - **Added:** `BiasCorrector` (BiC-style, 2 params per task-group: `logits_new -> alpha*logits_new + beta`, fit on held-out val/buffer, trunk+head frozen). Phase 0 exposes `fit_bic()` / `apply()` + `bias_correction` flag plumbing; full BiC training loop lands in Phase 1.
 391: - **Added:** `replay_balance="uniform"|"class_balanced"` — reservoir sampling over-represents the large T0 class pool; balanced interleaving is the known fix for new-class head bias. Default stays `uniform` so old numbers reproduce.
 392: - **Why:** reviewer P0.3 (joint bound mislabelled) + P4 (bias is the dominant CIL failure; EWC `lambda=0` already best on GRU/CNN in `ablation_ewc_lambda.csv`, so regularisation alone cannot fix logit competition).
 393: 
 394: ### 0.3 `src/cmmu.py` — herding selector + val-balanced Fisher guidance
 395: - **Added:** `HerdingBuffer.select_herding()` (per-class mean-matching exemplar selection) alongside existing reservoir `ReplayBuffer`; added `ReplayBuffer.sample_balanced()` for class-balanced minibatch augmentation.
 396: - **Added:** `OnlineEWC.consolidate(..., X_val=None)` — Fisher estimated on val-balanced sample when supplied; docstring warns against estimating Fisher on new-task train-only data (understates old-task curvature).
 397: - **Why:** iCaRL/BiC literature + reviewer P4; herding + balanced replay are prerequisites for Phase-1 `BiC / iCaRL-lite / LwF` baselines on CuCD-ID first, STIN second.

 458: ### 1.1 `src/train.py` — `lwf / bic / icarl` (all NumPy, CuCD-ID-first design)
 459: - **Added:** `_distill_dlogits` (Hinton KD gradient, T²-scaled, old-head columns only) + `_snapshot_teacher` (frozen trunk+old head before each growth step) + `_rebuild_herding_buffer` (equal exemplars/class, input-space herding — documented lite limitation vs embedding-space iCaRL).
 460: - `lwf`: memory-free distillation, no replay. `bic`: herding + balanced replay + distillation + full `(alpha,beta)` BiC grid fit on held-out val. `icarl` (lite): herding + balanced replay + distillation, softmax eval (NCM omitted — documented).
 461: - **Bug fixed during smoke test:** KD was first combined as convex `(1-lam)*CE + KD`, which at the default `distill_lambda=1.0` zeroed new-class learning (`lwf ACC~=chance`). Changed to additive `CE + lam*KD`; post-fix 3-epoch smoke (MLP/CuCD-ID): `bic 0.612 > full 0.415 ≈ replay 0.413 > icarl 0.326 > lwf 0.291`.
 462: - **Why:** reviewer P1.5 + base paper (BiC best, LwF/iCaRL family expected); tests stay on CuCD-ID first, STIN second — no generic dataset added per user constraint.

STIN must not use these (no benign) — `run_main.final_detection_metrics` returns NaN there.
 466: - **Added:** `wilcoxon_signed_rank` (normal approx with tie correction, no scipy) for matched-seed method pairs.
 467: - Smoke finding (3 epochs, unconverged): detection AUROC stays ~1.0 even when ACC collapses (collapsed head predicts everything as attack) while FPR95 separates (`replay 0.001` vs `lwf 0.738`) — confirms classification-vs-detection dissociation is a paper-worthy RQ, matching the base paper's take-home.
 468: - **Why:** IDS paper without normal-vs-attack evaluation is rejectable; stats required for Q1/Q2 (5 seeds → min two-sided p=0.0625, so effects reported alongside p).

   1: # Paper plan — resource-aware CIL for CubeSat IDS (simulation-only)
   2: 
   3: Positioning: not another CIL algorithm. Question: what do existing CIL
   4: strategies cost, and what do they return, under realistic onboard memory and
   5: uplink budgets? All evidence comes from rerunnable scripts:
   6: train → validation tuning → freeze (`best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`) →
   7: final test.
   8: 
   9: Primary backbone: MLP (tabular). GRU and 1-D CNN are compact architectural
  10: stress tests, not genuine temporal models. Datasets: CuCD-ID (Fayyaz et al.,
  11: Data in Brief 2026, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2026.112598; NOS3/cFS
  12: software-in-the-loop simulation) and STIN (Li et al., IEEE Access 2020,
  13: doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3041641). All CuCD-ID telemetry is simulated; neither
  14: dataset is a live-spacecraft capture.
  15: 
  16: ## RQs → evidence (all values generated from result files)
  17: 
  18: - RQ1 severity of forgetting: `main_results_summary.csv` and per-class
  19:   outputs show whether naive fine-tuning/EWC collapse and which classes
  20:   survive. Do not copy numbers into the manuscript; read the CSV at build time.
  21: - RQ2 which mechanism survives TinyML limits: `main_results_summary.csv` plus
  22:   `stats_permutation.csv` / `stats_permutation_macrof1.csv`. Report the full
  23:   per-backbone matrix and corrected paired tests; do not assume a single
  24:   pooled winner. Check whether replay+EWC beats replay per backbone.
  25: - RQ3 memory-stability tradeoff: `ablation_buffer_size.csv` and the memory
  26:   ledger. Report persistent and peak update memory separately.
  27: - RQ4 uplink budget: `fewshot.csv` (frozen configs, across K values) and
  28:   `consistency_check.json`. Read the knee from the generated table/figure;
  29:   report variability across seeds.
  30: - RQ5 task order: `task_order_disentangled.csv`. Report budget-mode means and
  31:   individual-run variability; the legacy confounded headline is retired.
  32: - RQ6 robustness: `robustness.csv` and `leakage_ablation_summary.csv`.
  33:   Distinguish test-time corruptions from retrained feature-group ablations.
  34:   Treat window/aggregate reliance as a leakage caveat, not deployment skill.
  35: - RQ7 simulated cost: persistent vs peak RAM, MAC/sample, MAC/update
  36:   (including replay/teacher), and host update seconds. Mark simulated costs
  37:   as not MCU-measured.
  38: - Detection vs classification: `DET_*` columns. Alarm quality and
  39:   class-incremental accuracy are separate outcomes.
  40: - Bounds: `temporal_purged_compare.csv`. IID and forward-temporal stress are
  41:   separate estimands; purge width is recorded in the CSV. Absent scenario IDs
  42:   prevent a group split; state this data-collection limitation.
  43: 
  44: ## Figures
  45: 
  46: All figures are regenerated by `analysis/plots.py`; the authoritative count is
  47: whatever that script writes and `final_experiment_manifest.json` records.
  48: Core set: method comparison with Macro-F1, forgetting curves, heatmaps,
  49: per-class F1, finetune-vs-iCaRL confusion, disentangled task-order plot,
  50: `fewshot_pareto.png`, `arch_tune.png`, `temporal_bracket.png`,
  51: `robustness.png`, and `leakage_ablation.png`.
  52: 
  53: ## Limits to state frankly
  54: 
  55: Random-split leakage (window aggregates/identifiers); retrained leakage
  56: ablation quantifies reliance, while test-time `nowindow` is not a leakage-free
  57: estimate. Temporal results are a stress estimand under drift with a
  58: T0-frozen scaler, not ground truth. Use Holm correction and effect sizes;
  59: never p-value-only claims. Costs are simulation-only (no MCU, no INT8
  60: kernels); STIN has no benign class; BiC-lite/iCaRL-lite are input-space
  61: herding variants without NCM; GRU/CNN are reshaped-tabular stress tests and
  62: are feature-order sensitive. EWC uses a class-balanced cumulative old+new
  63: validation Fisher with per-architecture tuned gamma weighting (a validation
  64: weight, not a decay factor). BiC/Fisher calibration data are counted inside
  65: the uplink budget. Purge can empty validation for narrow TimeRadians classes;
  66: this is warned, not silent.
  67: 
  68: ## Still open
  69: 
  70: Manuscript writing. Every CSV, figure, manifest, and report is regenerated by
  71: `run_all.py` before submission; the final report is written automatically by
  72: `experiments/generate_summary_report.py` from those files.

FILE: ./PROJECT_CONTEXT.md (19.4 KB)
================================================================================
   1: # PROJECT_CONTEXT.md
   2: ### Class-Incremental Continual Learning for TinyML-Based Intrusion Detection in CubeSats
   3: 
   4: This document describes what the project is and what has been implemented in the codebase. It intentionally excludes performance results, accuracy numbers, or outcome data — it is a reference for the problem, design, and implementation only.
   5: 
   6: ---
   7: 
   8: ## 1. One-paragraph summary
   9: 
  10: A from-scratch (pure NumPy, no PyTorch/TensorFlow/autograd) implementation of **class-incremental continual learning** for onboard, memory-constrained intrusion detection on CubeSats. The **MLP is the primary backbone** — it directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector. A compact GRU and 1-D CNN are evaluated as **architectural stress tests**, not genuine temporal sequence models. Nine continual-learning configurations (naive fine-tuning, replay, online EWC, combined replay+EWC, LwF, BiC-lite, iCaRL-lite, and two offline joint references) are compared under the strict class-incremental protocol: no task ID is ever available at inference time, and every sample is classified through a single, dynamically-growing shared softmax head. The pipeline enforces **train → validation tuning → freeze hyperparameters → final test**: test data is never used for hyperparameter selection.
  11: 
  12: ---
  13: 
  14: ## 2. Problem setting and operational concept
  15: 
  16: CubeSats running NASA's cFS flight software on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware face evolving cyber threats (command flooding, data injection, defence impairment, storage exhaustion). Deployed intrusion detection models are typically **static** — once launched, their weights are frozen, and adapting to a newly discovered attack normally requires re-uploading the full firmware image over a narrow 5–15 minute ground contact window.
  17: 
  18: The system modelled here instead assumes a **human-in-the-loop, edge-adaptation workflow**:
  19: 
  20: 1. **Space** — the onboard IDS flags anomalous telemetry and downlinks it.
  21: 2. **Earth** — a human analyst labels the new attack type.
  22: 3. **Earth → Space** — only a small labelled CSV (kilobytes, not megabytes) is uplinked.
  23: 4. **Space** — the model runs a short continual-learning update onboard, incorporating the new attack type without forgetting the attack types already learned.
  24: 
  25: This shifts the adaptation burden onto the edge hardware, avoids full firmware retransmission, and keeps a human in the loop for safety-critical security decisions.
  26: 
  27: ### Why class-incremental, not task-incremental
  28: 
  29: A **task-incremental** protocol (task ID known at inference time, one private output head per task) is the easier of the two standard continual-learning settings — the model only ever discriminates within a small, known subset of classes. It's a poor model of a real onboard IDS, since a real classifier has no oracle telling it in advance which subset of attacks a given packet could belong to — it must decide among *everything it has ever learned*, at once.
  30: 
  31: The codebase therefore implements the harder, more realistic **class-incremental** protocol: a single shared classification head grows by a few output columns every time a new attack type is introduced, and at evaluation time the model must select the correct class from *all* classes learned so far, with no side information about which task a sample came from.
  32: 
  33: ---
  34: 
  35: ## 3. Datasets
  36: 
  37: | Dataset | Role | Files | Rows | Features | Classes |
  38: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  39: | **CuCD-ID** | Primary | `noised_dataset.csv` | 22,465 | 22 (telemetry) | 5 (`normal`, `command_flooding`, `data_injection`, `defence_impairment`, `storage_exhaustion`) |
  40: | **STIN** | Secondary / cross-domain stress test | `SAT20.csv` + `TER20.csv` (concatenated) | 209,564 | 30 (network flow) | 9 attack types (`Syn_DDoS`, `UDP_DDoS`, `LDAP_DDoS`, `MSSQL_DDoS`, `Botnet`, `Portmap_DDoS`, `Web Attack`, `Backdoor`, `NetBIOS_DDoS`) |
  41: 
  42: **Provenance and scope.** CuCD-ID is the labelled NOS3/cFS CubeSat telemetry dataset of Fayyaz et al. (Data in Brief 2026, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2026.112598; Mendeley doi:10.17632/7n2d42pm3n.3). It was generated in a software-in-the-loop digital twin; all telemetry is simulated, not captured from an orbiting spacecraft. STIN (SAT20/TER20) is the satellite/terrestrial flow dataset of Li et al. (IEEE Access 2020, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3041641; github.com/kun9717/STIN-data-set). STIN has no benign/normal class in the provided files, so it is used purely as a larger-scale, higher-class-count cross-domain stress test. A coarse STIN/MLP sweep provides an initial hyperparameter prior only; final method × architecture hyperparameters are tuned on CuCD-ID validation data and frozen (`results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`) before any test evaluation.
  43: 
  44: ### Task construction (class-incremental protocol)
  45: 
  46: Every task introduces classes that have never appeared in any earlier task — classes are never repeated. There is a single shared classifier head; when a task is processed, `model.expand_head()` appends one new output column per new class, and every future prediction (on any task's test data) goes through the full, current-width head.
  47: 
  48: - **CuCD-ID → 4 tasks, 5 classes total**: `T0 = {normal, command_flooding}` (base task, 2 classes), then `T1 = {data_injection}`, `T2 = {defence_impairment}`, `T3 = {storage_exhaustion}` (1 new class each).
  49: - **STIN → 3 tasks, 9 classes total**: `T0 = {Syn_DDoS, UDP_DDoS, LDAP_DDoS}`, `T1 = {MSSQL_DDoS, Botnet, Portmap_DDoS}`, `T2 = {Web Attack, Backdoor, NetBIOS_DDoS}` (3 new classes per task).
  50: 
  51: **Uplink-budget-constrained training sets.** Reflecting the "small labelled CSV" operational constraint, task 0 of each dataset is trained on a larger pre-launch corpus (700 samples/class), while every subsequent task is trained on only 150 samples/class — modelling a realistically small ground-to-satellite uplink payload. Test sets are independent, held-out, and not subject to this budget. The reported uplink budget counts **adaptation data plus the onboard calibration data** consumed by BiC fitting and val-balanced Fisher estimation (packed INT8 payload estimates, excluding CSV text, scale/zero-point parameters, and protocol framing overhead).
  52: 
  53: **Fixed preprocessing.** A feature normalizer (mean/std) is fit only on task 0's training data and applied unchanged to every later task — modelling that onboard preprocessing configuration is fixed at launch and cannot be recalibrated using data from attacks not yet seen.
  54: 
  55: **Order-independent label handling.** Each task's labels are stored locally and resolved to the model's actual global head-column indices dynamically, based on the order tasks are processed in — this is what allows the task-order ablation to safely replay the same task sequence in a different order without corrupting label alignment.
  56: 
  57: ---
  58: 
  59: ## 4. Architectures (`src/models.py`)
  60: 
  61: All three backbones are implemented from scratch in NumPy, with hand-derived forward *and* backward passes (verified against finite-difference numerical gradient checks in `tests/test_gradients.py`, including growing-head gradient checks) and one shared, dynamically-growing classification head (`expand_head(n_new_classes)` appends new output columns while leaving existing ones untouched).
  62: 
  63: | Model | Trunk | Role |
  64: |---|---|---|
  65: | **CubeSat MLP** | `Linear(F,32) → ReLU → Linear(32,16) → ReLU` | **Primary backbone** — directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector. It has no imposed feature-order inductive bias, but empirical permutation invariance is not established by the two-seed exploratory study. |
  66: | **CubeSat GRU** | Single-layer GRU, hidden size 10 | **Architectural stress test** — feature vector reshaped into a pseudo-sequence (e.g. CuCD-ID's 22 features → 11 timesteps × 2 features), processed with full manual backpropagation-through-time. Not a genuine temporal model. |
  67: | **CubeSat 1-D CNN** | `Conv1D(1→6, k=3) → ReLU → Conv1D(6→10, k=3) → ReLU → GlobalAvgPool` | **Architectural stress test** — feature vector treated as a length-F, 1-channel signal; convolution implemented via an explicit, gradient-checked im2col-style loop. Sensitive to feature ordering. |
  68: 
  69: Each architecture is sized in the low hundreds to under two thousand parameters. Persistent deployment footprints are evaluated against an assumed 60 KB TinyML persistent-state budget (a conservative study constraint, not a universal hardware limit), reported separately from estimated peak update RAM.
  70: 
  71: ---
  72: 
  73: ## 5. CMMU — Continual Memory Management Unit (`src/cmmu.py`)
  74: 
  75: Two independent, combinable sub-mechanisms:
  76: 
  77: - **A) Experience Replay Buffer** — a fixed-capacity reservoir-sampling exemplar buffer. A fraction of every training minibatch after task 0 is drawn from the buffer, interleaving old-class examples with new-class examples. Deployed footprint is computed as int8-quantised bytes.
  78: - **B) Online EWC** — "Online" Elastic Weight Consolidation (Schwarz et al., 2018): a single running diagonal Fisher-information estimate and a single anchor-parameter snapshot are kept, giving O(1) memory in the number of tasks learned (unlike vanilla per-task EWC). The Fisher is estimated from a class-balanced mix of the current task's training data and the cumulative calibration pool of all tasks seen so far (not the current task alone), accumulated as `F_new = γ·F_old + F_current` with per-architecture EWC-only tuned γ weighting (MLP 0.5 / GRU 1.0 / CNN 0.5; γ is a validation-tuned weighting parameter, not a conventional decay factor). Because the classification head grows over time, the Fisher/anchor arrays are padded to the new shape as needed; newly-added output columns start with zero Fisher (unconstrained) until the task that introduced them is itself consolidated. Under the class-incremental protocol, the shared head is treated as equally susceptible to forgetting as the trunk, so EWC protects the whole model, head included.
  79: 
  80: Nine configurations are implemented for comparison: `finetune` (naive baseline), `replay` (A only), `ewc` (B only), `full` (A+B combined), `lwf` (distillation only, no memory), `bic-lite` and `icarl-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation; lite = resource-conscious variants with input-space herding, softmax eval, no NCM), `joint` (legacy cumulative warm-start, non-deployable), and `joint_scratch` (from-scratch retraining on accumulated data — an offline joint-training reference, not a strict upper bound).
  81: 
  82: ---
  83: 
  84: ## 6. Metrics implemented (`src/metrics.py`)
  85: 
  86: Standard continual-learning metrics computed from the full per-task accuracy matrix `R[i,j]` (accuracy on task `j`'s classes, decided among all classes known at that point via the single shared head, right after finishing training on task `i`):
  87: 
  88: - **ACC** — mean accuracy over all tasks after learning the final task.
  89: - **Macro-F1 (primary)** — class-balanced mean F1, computed from the final head with BiC correction applied when fitted.
  90: - **Balanced Accuracy** — mean per-class recall.
  91: - **BWT** — Backward Transfer (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, 2017); measures forgetting.
  92: - **FM** — Forgetting Measure (Chaudhry et al., 2018); mean drop from each task's peak accuracy to its final accuracy.
  93: 
  94: Additional metrics implemented:
  95: 
  96: - **Persistent deployment footprint** (int8 model weights + int8 replay + fp16 EWC state), reported separately from **estimated peak update RAM** (FP32 weights, gradients, Adam states, activations, batches, replay minibatch, teacher, temporary buffers).
  97: - **Estimated MACs** per forward pass and per performed training update (final-head-width proxy; conservative estimate, not hardware measurement).
  98: - **Per-class precision / recall / F1 / confusion matrix** (`confusion_matrix`, `per_class_prf1` functions), computed via `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py` — implemented specifically to make class-level forgetting directly visible rather than only implied by the aggregate task-level metrics.
  99: - **Headline statistics**: exact paired permutation tests with Holm correction, Cohen's d, and bootstrap 95% CIs (`experiments/run_stats.py`).
 100: 
 101: ---
 102: 
 103: ## 7. Experiments implemented (`experiments/`)
 104: 
 105: 1. **`run_hparam_sweep.py`** — a coarse 160-point grid search over the STIN dataset using the MLP backbone as a fast proxy, `method="full"`, scored only on the selection half of validation. The winner is a prior only, not the final configuration.
 106: 2. **`run_validation_tune.py`** — per-method × per-architecture validation tuning on CuCD-ID (9 methods × 3 architectures × 3 seeds; 2,268 seed-runs). Validation is 20% of each per-class pool, split 50/50 into disjoint calibration and selection halves: BiC/Fisher use calibration, while tuning scores only the selection half. Winners are frozen to `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` and used unchanged by every subsequent experiment; test data is never used for selection.
 107: 3. **`run_main.py`** — the full experiment matrix: 2 datasets × 3 architectures × 9 methods × 15 seeds = 810 runs, each producing a full accuracy matrix, CL + Macro-F1/Balanced-Accuracy metrics, detection metrics (CuCD-ID), training time, persistent vs peak memory accounting, and MAC estimates.
 108: 4. **Phase-2 evidence** — purged temporal evaluation (`run_purged_temporal.py`: 270 runs, IID vs forward-temporal with 0.02 rad TimeRadians purge, chronological unwrapping), few-shot uplink sweep (`run_fewshot.py`: 420 runs, K varies under fixed and scaled calibration protocols), exploratory feature-order permutation (`run_feature_order.py`: 96 runs, one split, two seeds; not a stability claim), disentangled task-order study (`run_task_order.py`: 144 runs, two-class-T0-first primary and single-class-first degenerate runs reported separately), ablations (`run_ablation.py`: 1,170 runs for buffer capacity and EWC lambda), per-class analysis (`run_per_class_analysis.py`: 1,890 rows, 15 seeds × 9 methods, BiC correction applied), exact permutation statistics on ACC and Macro-F1 (`run_stats.py`: 216 all-pairwise comparisons per metric, Holm across the full family), matched-replay/EWC controls (`run_baseline_controls.py`: 450 runs), robustness + simulated INT8 (`run_robustness.py`), a 225-run retrained feature-provenance leakage ablation (`run_leakage_ablation.py`), and the main-vs-fewshot consistency check (`check_consistency.py`).
 109: 5. **`analysis/plots.py`** — generates all 21 figures (method comparison with Macro-F1, accuracy heatmaps, buffer/lambda sensitivity, confusion matrices, forgetting curves, per-class F1, task-order sensitivity, memory footprint, hyperparameter sweep heatmap, few-shot Pareto, temporal bracket, robustness).
 110: 6. **`create_manifest.py` + `generate_summary_report.py`** — write `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` (machine-readable provenance) and auto-generate `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` plus `v6_2_project_report_final.md` by pulling every number directly from the CSV/JSON result files (no hand-typed values anywhere in the reporting pipeline).
 111: 
 112: ---
 113: 
 114: ## 8. Correctness verification implemented
 115: 
 116: - **`tests/test_gradients.py`** — numerical (finite-difference) gradient checking of every hand-derived backward pass (MLP, GRU, CNN1D), including the growing-head case, to confirm the from-scratch backpropagation implementation is mathematically correct rather than merely plausible-looking.
 117: - **Dataset integrity**: checksum verification for raw and processed dataset files.
 118: - **Data-leakage prevention**: train/test split performed before any scaling/normalization; the fixed-at-task-0 normalizer is deliberately never refit on later tasks' data.
 119: 
 120: ---

 163: 
 164: ## 10. What is implemented vs. not yet implemented
 165: 
 166: **Implemented:**
 167: - Full data pipeline for both datasets, with 4-task (CuCD-ID) / 3-task (STIN) class-incremental splits in three protocols: IID random, temporal, and temporal-purged (0.02 rad TimeRadians purge).
 168: - All three TinyML architectures, hand-derived and gradient-verified (MLP primary; GRU/CNN as stress tests).
 169: - Nine CIL configurations including LwF, BiC-lite, iCaRL-lite, and two offline joint references, with stage-local BiC, bounded herding, and teacher snapshotting.
 170: - Validation-based per-method/architecture tuning with disjoint calibration/selection halves and frozen configs; 810-run main matrix (15 seeds); full Phase-2 evidence (temporal, few-shot with calibration-counted uplink, feature-order, task-order, ablations, per-class, 216-comparison exact permutation stats with Holm, matched controls, robustness with simulated INT8).
 171: - Persistent vs peak-update-RAM accounting, performed-counter MAC estimates, main-vs-fewshot consistency checking, machine-readable experiment manifest.
 172: - Automated, reproducible results/report/figure generation (no hand-typed numbers); legacy outputs quarantined under `results/legacy/`.
 173: 
 174: **Not yet implemented:**
 175: - Per-class precision/recall/F1 analysis for the remaining architecture/dataset combinations beyond the two headline configurations.
 176: - Onboard training time / power draw / SRAM measurement on flight-representative hardware (current costs are host-estimated; training runs in NumPy on a standard CPU; INT8 is a simulated round-trip proxy).
 177: - An onboard novelty/anomaly-detection mechanism to trigger the "new attack detected" alert in the first place — the pipeline assumes this alert and its labelled data already exist.
 178: - Calibration-free onboard updates (current BiC/Fisher consume uplink-counted calibration data by design, Option A).

FILE: ./README.md (31.7 KB)
================================================================================
   1: # Class-Incremental Continual Learning for TinyML CubeSat Intrusion Detection
   2: 
   3: A from-scratch (pure NumPy, no PyTorch/TensorFlow) implementation and full
   4: experimental evaluation of **class-incremental continual learning** for
   5: onboard, memory-constrained intrusion detection on
   6: CubeSats. The **MLP is the primary backbone** -- it directly processes the
   7: tabular telemetry feature vector. A compact GRU and 1-D CNN are evaluated as
   8: **architectural stress tests**, not as genuine temporal sequence models (the
   9: inputs are tabular feature vectors, not raw telemetry sequences). Nine
  10: continual-learning configurations (replay, online EWC, LwF, BiC-lite,
  11: iCaRL-lite, combined replay+EWC, naive fine-tuning, and two offline joint
  12: references) are compared under the strict **class-incremental**
  13: protocol: no task ID is ever available at inference time, and every sample
  14: must be classified by a single, dynamically-growing shared softmax head.
  15: 
  16: **Scope and claims.** This repository is a resource-aware benchmark and
  17: negative-result study, not a claim that the combined `full` method wins. The
  18: IID split is a benchmark estimand; temporal-purged and feature-provenance
  19: results are separate validity checks.
  20: 
  21: This repository contains the full codebase; running `python3 run_all.py`
  22: reproduces every number and figure referenced below directly from the
  23: provided CSV data (no placeholder or hand-typed results anywhere in the
  24: pipeline). The pipeline enforces **train → validation tuning → freeze
  25: hyperparameters → final test**: no test data is ever used for
  26: hyperparameter selection.
  27: 
  28: ---
  29: 
  30: ## 1. Problem setting and operational concept
  31: 
  32: CubeSats running NASA's cFS on COTS hardware face evolving cyber threats
  33: (command flooding, data injection, defence impairment, storage exhaustion,
  34: network-layer DDoS, etc.). Deployed IDS models are typically **static**:
  35: once launched, their weights are frozen, and adapting to a newly discovered
  36: attack requires re-uploading the full firmware image over a narrow
  37: 5-15 minute uplink window.
  38: 
  39: The system modelled here instead assumes a **human-in-the-loop, edge
  40: adaptation** workflow:
  41: 
  42: 1. **Space** -- the onboard IDS flags anomalous telemetry and downlinks it.
  43: 2. **Earth** -- a human analyst labels the new attack type.
  44: 3. **Earth -> Space** -- only a *small* labelled CSV (kilobytes, not
  45:    megabytes) is uplinked.
  46: 4. **Space** -- the model runs a short continual-learning update onboard,
  47:    incorporating the new attack type **without forgetting** the attack
  48:    types learned so far.
  49: 
  50: This shifts the adaptation burden onto the edge hardware, eliminates the
  51: need for full firmware retransmission, and keeps a human in the loop for
  52: safety-critical security decisions.
  53: 
  54: ### Why class-incremental, not task-incremental
  55: 
  56: A **task-incremental** protocol (task ID known at inference time, one
  57: private output head per task) is the easier of the two standard continual-
  58: learning protocols: the model is only ever asked to discriminate within a
  59: small, known subset of classes. It is a poor model of an onboard IDS,
  60: though, because a real classifier has no oracle telling it in advance
  61: "this packet is either normal or a command-flood, nothing else" -- it must
  62: decide among *everything it has ever learned* at once.
  63: 
  64: This repository therefore implements the harder, more realistic
  65: **class-incremental** protocol: a single shared classification head grows
  66: by a few output columns every time a new attack type is introduced, and at
  67: evaluation time the model must pick the correct class out of *all* classes
  68: learned so far, with no side information about which task a sample came
  69: from. This exposes the well-known **class-incremental collapse** /
  70: "task-recency bias" failure mode -- softmax cross-entropy on a new class's
  71: samples actively pushes down the logits of every previously-learned class,
  72: even without any weight drift -- which a task-incremental evaluation would
  73: never surface. Section 7 shows this failure mode occurring, and the CMMU's
  74: (partial) mitigation of it, directly in the computed results.
  75: 
  76: ---
  77: 
  78: ## 2. Datasets
  79: 
  80: | Dataset | Role | Files | Rows | Features | Classes |
  81: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  82: | **CuCD-ID** | Primary | `data/CuCD-ID/noised_dataset.csv` | 22,465 | 22 (telemetry) | 5 (`normal`, `command_flooding`, `data_injection`, `defence_impairment`, `storage_exhaustion`) |
  83: | **STIN** | Secondary / cross-domain stress test | `data/STIN/SAT20.csv` + `TER20.csv` (concatenated) | 209,564 | 30 (network flow) | 9 distinct attack types (`Syn_DDoS`, `UDP_DDoS`, `LDAP_DDoS`, `MSSQL_DDoS`, `Botnet`, `Portmap_DDoS`, `Web Attack`, `Backdoor`, `NetBIOS_DDoS`) |
  84: 
  85: **Provenance and scope.** CuCD-ID is the labelled NOS3/cFS CubeSat
  86: telemetry dataset of Fayyaz et al., *Data in Brief* (2026),
  87: doi:10.1016/j.dib.2026.112598 (data: Mendeley
  88: doi:10.17632/7n2d42pm3n.3). It was generated in a high-fidelity
  89: software-in-the-loop digital twin; **all telemetry is simulated, not
  90: captured from an orbiting spacecraft**. STIN (SAT20/TER20) is the
  91: satellite/terrestrial flow dataset of Li et al., *IEEE Access* (2020),
  92: doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3041641 (github.com/kun9717/STIN-data-set). STIN
  93: has no benign/normal class in the provided files, so it is used purely
  94: as a larger-scale, higher-class-count **cross-domain stress test** to check
  95: whether findings generalize beyond the primary dataset. A coarse STIN/MLP
  96: sweep provides an initial hyperparameter prior only; **final
  97: method × architecture hyperparameters are tuned on CuCD-ID validation data
  98: and frozen** (`results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`) before any test
  99: evaluation -- the primary dataset's test numbers are never used for tuning.
 100: 
 101: **Leakage caveat.** CuCD-ID includes a circular time field, CCSDS packet
 102: identifiers, and 20-second sliding-window aggregates. The headline IID
 103: random split can share overlapping windows between train and test, so those
 104: numbers are benchmark estimates, not deployment guarantees. The
 105: `leakage_ablation` experiment retrains models after removing each feature
 106: group, and the temporal-purged protocol is reported separately; neither
 107: turns the IID number into a leakage-free estimate.
 108: 
 109: ### Task construction (class-incremental protocol)
 110: 
 111: Every task introduces a set of classes that have **never appeared in any
 112: earlier task** -- classes are never repeated. There is a single shared
 113: classifier head; when a task is processed, `model.expand_head()` appends
 114: one new output column per new class, and every future prediction (on any
 115: task's test data) goes through the full, current-width head. Full logic is
 116: in `src/data_utils.py` and `src/train.py`.
 117: 
 118: * **CuCD-ID -> 4 tasks, 5 classes total**:
 119:   `T0_launch = {normal, command_flooding}` (2 new classes -- a valid
 120:   classifier needs at least 2 classes to start from), then
 121:   `T1 = {data_injection}`, `T2 = {defence_impairment}`,
 122:   `T3 = {storage_exhaustion}` (1 new class each).
 123: * **STIN -> 3 tasks, 9 classes total**: `T0 = {Syn_DDoS, UDP_DDoS,
 124:   LDAP_DDoS}`, `T1 = {MSSQL_DDoS, Botnet, Portmap_DDoS}`,
 125:   `T2 = {Web Attack, Backdoor, NetBIOS_DDoS}` (3 new classes per task).
 126: 
 127: **Uplink-budget-constrained training sets.** Reflecting the "small labelled
 128: CSV" operational constraint, task 0 of each dataset is trained on a larger
 129: pre-launch corpus (700 samples/class), while every *subsequent* task is
 130: trained on only 150 samples/class -- a realistically small uplink payload.
 131: Test sets are independent, held-out, and **not** subject to this budget
 132: (they represent a ground-truth evaluation archive, never uplinked). Section
 133: 4 of `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` reports the exact computed uplink payload
 134: size in KB for every task: adaptation payload (raw float32 and packed int8)
 135: **plus** the onboard calibration payload consumed by BiC fitting and
 136: val-balanced Fisher estimation, with the combined total as the reported
 137: uplink budget. Payload figures are **packed telemetry payload estimates**
 138: (rows × features plus label bytes), excluding CSV text formatting,
 139: quantization scale/zero-point parameters, and packet/protocol framing
 140: overhead.
 141: 
 142: A feature normalizer (mean/std) is fit **only** on task 0's training data of
 143: each dataset and then applied unchanged to every later task -- modelling
 144: that the onboard preprocessing configuration is fixed at launch and cannot
 145: be recalibrated using data from attacks that haven't been seen yet.
 146: 
 147: **Order-independent label handling.** Each `Task`'s labels are stored
 148: *locally* (0..n_new_classes-1); `src/train.py` resolves them to the model's
 149: actual global head-column indices dynamically, based on the order tasks are
 150: *actually processed in*. This is what lets the task-order-sensitivity
 151: ablation safely replay the very same `TaskSequence` in a different order
 152: without corrupting label alignment (see `experiments/run_task_order.py`).

 155: 
 156: ## 3. Architectures
 157: 
 158: All three backbones are implemented from scratch in NumPy
 159: (`src/models.py`) with hand-derived forward *and* backward passes
 160: (verified against finite-difference gradients in `tests/test_gradients.py`,
 161: including growing-head gradient checks) and **one** shared, dynamically
 162: growing classification head (`expand_head(n_new_classes)` appends new
 163: output columns while leaving existing ones untouched).
 164: 
 165: | Model | Trunk | Role |
 166: |---|---|---|
 167: | **CubeSat MLP** | `Linear(F,32) -> ReLU -> Linear(32,16) -> ReLU` | **Primary backbone** -- directly processes the tabular telemetry feature vector. |
 168: | **CubeSat GRU** | Single-layer GRU, hidden size 10 | **Architectural stress test** -- feature vector reshaped into a pseudo-sequence (e.g. CuCD-ID's 22 features -> 11 timesteps x 2 features) and processed with full manual BPTT. Not a genuine temporal model. |
 169: | **CubeSat 1-D CNN** | `Conv1D(1->6,k=3) -> ReLU -> Conv1D(6->10,k=3) -> ReLU -> GlobalAvgPool` | **Architectural stress test** -- feature vector treated as a length-F, 1-channel signal; conv implemented via an explicit (correct, gradient-checked) im2col-style loop. Not genuine sequence modelling. |
 170: 
 171: A feature-order permutation study (`experiments/run_feature_order.py`)
 172: supports this framing only as an exploratory check: the MLP has **no imposed
 173: feature-order inductive bias**, but retraining under a permutation is not
 174: mathematically invariant. The study uses one data split and two training
 175: seeds (96 runs total), so it does not estimate a stable permutation effect.
 176: The CNN and GRU move more materially because convolution/recurrence depend on
 177: the imposed ordering. Read the generated feature-order table for the actual
 178: spread rather than assuming permutation invariance.
 179: 
 180: All configurations fit within the **assumed 60 KB TinyML persistent-state
 181: budget** imposed as a conservative study constraint (not a universal
 182: CubeSat hardware limit) -- see the generated memory ledger for the current
 183: largest configuration. Peak update RAM (FP32 weights, gradients, Adam
 184: states, **batch-32** activations, replay/teacher, and retained
 185: cumulative calibration state for EWC/full/BiC) is reported separately and is
 186: substantially larger. The cumulative calibration pool is update-time state,
 187: not deployed inference state; keeping it while fitting EWC/BiC/Fisher adds
 188: roughly 70.3 KB for CuCD-ID (750 calibration rows x 22 features x 4 bytes plus labels, as built), so persistent and
 189: update footprints are never conflated.
 190: 
 191: ---
 192: 
 193: ## 4. CMMU -- Continual Memory Management Unit (`src/cmmu.py`)
 194: 
 195: Two independent, combinable sub-mechanisms:
 196: 
 197: * **A) Experience Replay Buffer** -- fixed-capacity reservoir-sampling
 198:   exemplar buffer. A fraction of every training minibatch after task 0 is
 199:   drawn from the buffer, interleaving old-class examples with new-class
 200:   examples. Deployed footprint is computed as int8-quantised bytes.
 201: * **B) Online EWC** -- "Online" Elastic Weight Consolidation (Schwarz et
 202:   al., 2018): a *single* running diagonal Fisher-information estimate and
 203:   a *single* anchor-parameter snapshot are kept (O(1) memory in the number
 204:   of tasks learned, unlike vanilla per-task EWC, which is essential under
 205:   a fixed onboard memory budget). The Fisher is estimated from a
 206:   class-balanced mix of the current task's training data and the cumulative
 207:   calibration pool of all tasks seen so far (not the current task alone),
 208:   accumulated as `F_new = gamma * F_old + F_current` with per-architecture
 209:   EWC-only tuned weighting (frozen configs: MLP `gamma = 0.5`, GRU
 210:   `gamma = 1.0`, CNN `gamma = 0.5`). Here `gamma` is treated as a
 211:   validation-tuned weighting parameter rather than a conventional decay
 212:   factor; the combined `full` configuration is tuned separately.
 213:   Under the
 214:   class-incremental protocol, the shared head is just as susceptible to
 215:   forgetting as the trunk (the logit-competition effect described above),
 216:   so **EWC here protects the whole model, head included** -- unlike a
 217:   task-incremental design where disjoint per-task heads would need no such
 218:   protection. Because the head grows in width over time, the Fisher/anchor
 219:   arrays are padded to the new shape as needed; newly-added output columns
 220:   start with zero Fisher (unconstrained) until the task that introduced
 221:   them is itself consolidated.
 222: 
 223: Nine configurations are evaluated: `finetune`, `replay` (A only), `ewc`
 224: (B only), `full` (A+B combined), `lwf` (distillation only, no memory),
 225: `bic-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation + post-hoc bias
 226: correction), `icarl-lite` (herding + balanced replay + distillation,
 227: softmax classifier -- embedding-space herding and NCM evaluation omitted),
 228: `joint` (legacy cumulative warm-start, non-deployable), and
 229: `joint_scratch` (from-scratch retraining on accumulated data, an offline
 230: joint-training reference -- not a strict upper bound, since warm-start
 231: joint can exceed it). The `-lite` suffix marks resource-conscious variants,
 232: not exact reproductions of the original papers.
 233: 
 234: **Validation/calibration accounting (Option A).** The validation pool is
 235: split into two **disjoint** halves per task/class: calibration (BiC fitting
 236: and the EWC Fisher mix) and selection (hyperparameter scoring only). Because
 237: the onboard update is defined to reproduce these results, calibration samples
 238: are **counted inside the reported uplink budget**: payload figures are
 239: adaptation data + calibration data (`uplink_KB_total_with_calib` in
 240: `fewshot.csv`, §4 table totals). The selection half is an experimental
 241: scoring artifact and is excluded from the onboard budget. The alternative --
 242: a calibration-free onboard update -- is out of scope.
 243: 
 244: ---
 245: 
 246: ## 5. Metrics
 247: 
 248: Standard continual-learning metrics computed from the full per-task
 249: accuracy matrix `R[i,j]` = accuracy on task `j`'s classes (decided among
 250: *all* classes known at that point, via the single shared head) right after
 251: finishing training on task `i` (`src/metrics.py`):
 252: 
 253: * **ACC** -- mean accuracy over all tasks after learning the final task.
 254: * **Macro-F1 (primary)** -- class-balanced mean F1 over all classes seen so
 255:   far, computed from the final head with BiC correction applied when fitted.
 256: * **Balanced Accuracy** -- mean per-class recall.
 257: * **BWT** -- backward transfer (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, 2017); negative =
 258:   forgetting.
 259: * **FM** -- forgetting measure (Chaudhry et al., 2018): mean drop from each
 260:   task's peak accuracy to its final accuracy.
 261: 
 262: Plus persistent deployment footprint (int8 model + int8 replay + fp16 EWC
 263: state) reported **separately** from estimated peak update RAM (FP32
 264: weights, gradients, Adam states, activations, batches, replay minibatch,
 265: teacher where applicable, temporary buffers), per-sample and per-update MAC
 266: estimates (the shared head's compute cost grows as more classes are
 267: learned), and a **per-class precision / recall / F1 / confusion-matrix**
 268: breakdown (`confusion_matrix`, `per_class_prf1` in `src/metrics.py`)
 269: computed by `experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py`. The task-level metrics
 270: above only *imply* that specific classes get forgotten; the per-class
 271: breakdown makes it directly visible (e.g. an old class's F1 collapsing to
 272: 0.000) and is the more "visceral" evidence a CL paper reviewer typically
 273: expects to see alongside the aggregate numbers.
 274: 
 275: Headline method comparisons use **exact paired permutation tests with Holm
 276: correction**, reported with mean difference, 95% CI, and Cohen's d
 277: (`experiments/run_stats.py`) -- never p-values alone. The pre-specified
 278: family is **216 all-pairwise comparisons per metric** (all unordered method
 279: pairs within each dataset x architecture), with Holm applied across the full
 280: family. Current confirmatory results: **162/216 ACC** and **164/216
 281: Macro-F1** comparisons significant. Matched-replay and EWC-lambda controls
 282: are reported separately (`results/stats_baseline_controls.csv`; 7/30 survive
 283: Holm). These tests are exploratory, not winner-selected.
 284: 
 285: ---
 286: 
 287: ## 6. Experiments run
 288: 
 289: 1. **`experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py`** -- a 160-point grid search
 290:    (learning rate x EWC lambda x replay-buffer capacity x replay fraction)
 291:    over the **STIN** dataset using the MLP backbone as a fast proxy and
 292:    `method="full"`, scored on the **selection half** of validation
 293:    (`ACC_select - max(FM_select, 0)`, `val_frac=0.20`, disjoint from the
 294:    calibration half). The winner is a coarse prior only
 295:    (`results/best_hparams.json`).
 296: 2. **`experiments/run_validation_tune.py`** -- per-method x per-architecture
 297:    validation tuning on **CuCD-ID** (9 methods x 3 architectures x 3
 298:    seeds), scored only on the selection half. Winners are frozen to
 299:    `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json` and used, unchanged, by
 300:    every subsequent experiment -- test data is never used for selection.
 301: 3. **`experiments/run_main.py`** -- the full matrix: 2 datasets x 3
 302:    architectures x 9 methods (`finetune`/`replay`/`ewc`/`full`/`lwf`/
 303:    `bic`/`icarl`/`joint`/`joint_scratch`) x 15 seeds = **810 runs**, each
 304:    producing a full accuracy matrix, CL + Macro-F1/Balanced-Accuracy
 305:    metrics, detection metrics (CuCD-ID), training time, persistent vs peak
 306:    memory accounting and MACs estimates.
 307: 4. **Phase-2 evidence** -- purged temporal evaluation
 308:    (`run_purged_temporal.py`: IID vs forward-temporal with a 0.02 rad
 309:    TimeRadians purge), few-shot uplink sweep (`run_fewshot.py`: K =
 310:    5..300 under fixed and scaled calibration protocols), exploratory feature-order permutation
 311:    (`run_feature_order.py`), disentangled task-order study
 312:    (`run_task_order.py`: two-class-T0-first primary, single-class-first
 313:    degenerate runs reported separately), ablations
 314:    (`run_ablation.py`: buffer capacity, EWC lambda, legacy task order),
 315:    per-class analysis (`run_per_class_analysis.py`: frozen configs, BiC
 316:    correction applied), exact permutation statistics on **ACC and
 317:    Macro-F1** (`run_stats.py`), robustness + quantization + memory ledger
 318:    (`run_robustness.py`: simulated INT8 round-trip `int8_sim`), and a
 319:    feature-provenance leakage ablation (`run_leakage_ablation.py`:
 320:    retrain without time/identifier/window groups).
 321: 5. **`experiments/check_consistency.py`** -- verifies main vs few-shot
 322:    (K=150, intersecting seeds) hyperparameter and seed consistency.
 323: 6. **`analysis/plots.py`** -- generates every figure in `figures/`
 324:    (21 PNGs, Macro-F1 primary, three-protocol temporal bracket, leakage ablation).
 325: 7. **`experiments/create_manifest.py`** -- writes
 326:    `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` (machine-readable provenance).
 327: 8. **`experiments/generate_summary_report.py`** -- writes
 328:    `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` and `v6_2_project_report_final.md`, fully
 329:    auto-generated reports pulling every number directly out of the
 330:    CSV/JSON result files.
 331: 
 332: ### Run order and expected outputs (for running on your own machine)
 333: 
 334: ```bash
 335: pip install -r requirements.txt
 336: python3 run_all.py
 337: ```
 338: 
 339: or step by step (`python3 run_all.py --no-phase2` skips Phase-2):
 340: 
 341: ```bash
 342: python3 tests/test_gradients.py                    # sanity check
 343: python3 experiments/run_hparam_sweep.py             # STIN coarse prior (validation-scored)
 344: python3 experiments/run_validation_tune.py          # per-method/arch tuning (validation, frozen)
 345: python3 experiments/run_main.py                     # 810-run matrix (test evaluation only)
 346: python3 experiments/run_purged_temporal.py          # IID vs purged-temporal
 347: python3 experiments/run_fewshot.py                  # uplink sweep
 348: python3 experiments/run_feature_order.py            # exploratory feature-order permutation
 349: python3 experiments/run_task_order.py               # disentangled task order
 350: python3 experiments/run_ablation.py                 # buffer / lambda / order ablations
 351: python3 experiments/run_per_class_analysis.py       # per-class F1 + confusion matrices
 352: python3 experiments/run_stats.py                    # ACC + Macro-F1 permutation stats + Holm
 353: python3 experiments/run_robustness.py               # robustness + simulated INT8
 354: python3 experiments/run_leakage_ablation.py         # retrained feature-group leakage ablation
 355: python3 experiments/check_consistency.py            # main-vs-fewshot verification
 356: python3 analysis/plots.py                           # figures
 357: python3 experiments/create_manifest.py              # reproducibility manifest
 358: python3 experiments/generate_summary_report.py      # report
 359: ```
 360: 
 361: `python3 run_all.py` runs all of the above **in this exact order** and
 362: stops immediately if any step fails. The order matters: everything after
 363: validation tuning reads `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`; the
 364: plotting, manifest, and report steps read the CSV/JSON files written by
 365: every step before them.
 366: 
 367: Every step writes its outputs directly to `results/` (CSV/JSON) and, for
 368: the plotting step, `figures/` (PNG) -- both directories already exist in
 369: this repository (with the outputs from our own run included) and will
 370: simply be overwritten in place; nothing needs to be created by hand. After
 371: a full run you should have:
 372: 
 373: | File | Written by |
 374: |---|---|
 375: | `results/best_hparams.json`, `results/hparam_sweep_stin.csv` | sweep |
 376: | `results/best_hparams_per_method_arch.json`, `results/validation_tuning_results.csv` | validation tuning |
 377: | `results/main_results_runs.csv`, `results/main_results_summary.csv`, `results/accuracy_matrices.json` | main matrix |
 378: | `results/temporal_purged_compare.csv` | purged temporal |
 379: | `results/fewshot.csv` | few-shot uplink sweep |
 380: | `results/feature_order_stability.csv` | exploratory feature-order permutation |
 381: | `results/task_order_disentangled.csv` | task-order study |
 382: | `results/ablation_buffer_size.csv`, `results/ablation_ewc_lambda.csv`, `results/ablation_task_order.csv` | ablations |
 383: | `results/per_class_f1_runs.csv`, `results/per_class_f1_summary.csv`, `results/confusion_matrices.json` | per-class analysis |
 384: | `results/stats_permutation.csv`, `results/stats_permutation_macrof1.csv` | permutation stats (ACC + Macro-F1) |
 385: | `results/robustness.csv`, `results/memory_ledger.csv`, `results/activation_memory_ledger.csv` | robustness |
 386: | `results/leakage_ablation.csv`, `results/leakage_ablation_summary.csv` | leakage ablation |
 387: | `results/final_experiment_manifest.json` | manifest |
 388: | 21 PNG files under `figures/` | plots |
 389: | `results/baseline_controls.csv`, `results/stats_baseline_controls.csv` | equal-buffer / EWC-lambda controls |
 390: | `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`, `v6_2_project_report_final.md` | report |
 391: 
 392: Nothing needs network access at run time (the two datasets are already
 393: included under `data/`); everything is deterministic given the fixed seeds
 394: in `experiments/config.py` (main matrix: seeds 0-14; few-shot: 0-4;
 395: validation tuning: 0-2), so re-running the whole pipeline should
 396: reproduce every number in `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` and every figure
 397: exactly.
 398: 
 399: (Full pipeline: about 4 hours on 4 CPU cores with `CL_JOBS=4`; the
 400: confirmatory run measured 3h59m compute / 4h07m wall, dominated by validation
 401: tuning, the 810-run matrix, and ablations. No GPU required.)
 402: 
 403: ---
 404: 
 405: ## 7. Headline results
 406: 
 407: Every result value is written by the experiment pipeline; none is edited by
 408: hand. See `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` and the auto-generated
 409: `v6_2_project_report_final.md` for the current tables, confidence intervals,
 410: paired tests, ablations, and figures. `results/main_results_summary.csv` is
 411: the underlying source for the headline matrix.
 412: 
 413: The supported qualitative findings are:
 414: 
 415: - Class-incremental naive fine-tuning collapses on the sequential benchmark;
 416:   EWC/LwF alone do not rescue it.
 417: - Replay and replay-based methods substantially reduce forgetting, but their
 418:   ranking depends on architecture and tuning; report the per-backbone matrix,
 419:   not a single pooled winner.
 420: - The combined EWC+replay+BiC (`full`) configuration is **not** a uniform
 421:   improvement over replay. On CuCD-ID it is below replay for all three
 422:   architectures; treat it as a baseline, not the proposed winner.
 423: - BiC-lite and iCaRL-lite are competitive with replay on several backbones,
 424:   while the offline joint references define the ceiling.
 425: - The STIN cross-domain stress test has a much lower ceiling than CuCD-ID.
 426: - Architecture matters: MLP is the primary backbone, with GRU/CNN treated as
 427:   stress tests rather than assumed equivalents.
 428: - The IID split is a benchmark estimand. Temporal-purged evaluation and
 429:   feature-provenance ablations are separate reliance/robustness estimands and
 430:   are not deployment accuracy claims.
 431: - Persistent model memory fits the assumed budget, but estimated peak update
 432:   RAM is materially larger and is reported separately.
 433: 
 434: Task-order variation, per-class collapse, robustness, leakage, power, and
 435: significance details are all generated from the corresponding CSV/JSON files;
 436: consult those files rather than copying numbers into prose.
 437: 
 438: ---

 484: ## 9. Limitations and threats to validity
 485: 
 486: * **No hardware-in-the-loop measurement.** Latency and memory are
 487:   host-estimated (per-sample/per-update MAC estimates, analytic byte
 488:   counts); no measurement was taken on actual Cortex-M-class silicon, no
 489:   INT8 kernels were executed (quantization is a simulated round-trip
 490:   proxy), and wall-clock NumPy timings are not reported as latency
 491:   figures. All such quantities carry `SIM_` prefixes or "estimated"
 492:   qualifiers where applicable.
 493: * **STIN has no benign class** in the provided extract, so it cannot be
 494:   used to evaluate normal-vs-attack detection directly, only inter-attack
 495:   class-incremental discrimination; it is used as a cross-domain stress
 496:   test only (the coarse STIN sweep is a prior, not the final tuning). Its
 497:   joint/offline accuracy ceiling is notably lower than CuCD-ID's,
 498:   indicating the 9-class discrimination problem is
 499:   intrinsically harder at this feature set and scale -- not merely a
 500:   continual-learning artefact.
 501: * **GRU/CNN are architectural stress tests, not temporal models.** Both
 502:   operate on reshaped tabular feature vectors, not genuine sequences. The
 503:   exploratory feature-order study moves more for GRU/CNN, but it does not
 504:   establish that the MLP is permutation-invariant (one split, two training
 505:   seeds). GRU is also one of the two architectures (with CNN1D)
 506:   most sensitive to EWC lambda -- confirmed on **both** CuCD-ID and STIN
 507:   independently (Section 7 / `results/RESULTS_SUMMARY.md` Section 5.2) --
 508:   reported as a finding, not adjusted away.
 509: * **CNN1D underperforms on CuCD-ID** relative to MLP/GRU even after
 510:   per-method validation tuning (see the generated main-results matrix), and degrades
 511:   under feature permutation; the residual gap (optimization + structural
 512:   sensitivity) is reported as an open question rather than resolved.
 513: * **Small task sample counts** (deliberately, to respect the KB-scale
 514:   uplink constraint) mean per-seed variance can be non-trivial for some
 515:   configurations (see the std columns in `results/main_results_runs.csv`
 516:   and the buffer-size/task-order ablations); all headline numbers are
 517:   reported as means over 15 seeds with 95% CIs and effect sizes for key
 518:   comparisons.
 519: * **Empirical Fisher from the cumulative calibration pool.** Online EWC
 520:   here uses the empirical Fisher (squared gradient of the true-label
 521:   log-likelihood, estimated from a class-balanced mix of current-task
 522:   training data and the cumulative calibration pool, with the running
 523:   estimate retained) rather than the exact expected Fisher over old-task
 524:   data; EWC-only per-architecture tuned decay applies (MLP 0.5 / GRU 1.0 /
 525:   CNN 0.5).
 526: * **Calibration and selection are disjoint.** BiC/Fisher use the calibration
 527:   half; hyperparameter scoring uses the selection half. Validation is
 528:   therefore not untouched by model fitting, but test data is. Calibration
 529:   samples are counted inside the reported uplink budget; selection samples
 530:   are experimental-only and excluded (see Section 2).
 531: * **Task-order effect is non-trivial and unexplained in mechanism.** The
 532:   disentangled study reports budget-mode means and per-order spread in the
 533:   generated task-order table; individual runs vary more still. On primary
 534:   orders, `fixed_position` and `moves_with_task` are identical by construction
 535:   because every primary order starts with T0, so they are not independent
 536:   evidence. Whether the remaining variation is class difficulty or order
 537:   interaction is flagged as future work rather than resolved here.
 538: * **Temporal evaluation is a stress estimand, not ground truth.** The
 539:   purged protocol reduces window overlap (0.02 rad TimeRadians purge) but
 540:   the data also exhibits mission-time drift and a T0-frozen scaler. The
 541:   temporal-purged arm falls to roughly four-class chance, and the stricter
 542:   no-leaky arm can fall below it; IID and temporal numbers are separate
 543:   regimes, and IID is not a deployment guarantee.
 544: * **No true scenario-level validation is possible.** CuCD-ID has no
 545:   scenario/run identifier in the released CSV. A grouped time-block proxy is
 546:   a sensitivity estimand only.
 547: * **Hyperparameters transfer across datasets and tuning/evaluation seeds
 548:   overlap.** All final configs are tuned on CuCD-ID validation; STIN is a
 549:   cross-dataset transfer test. Tuning seeds 0-2 overlap confirmatory seeds
 550:   0-14. Selection is validation-only (no test leakage), but the seeds are not
 551:   fully independent.
 552: * **Feature-order evidence is exploratory.** The study uses one split and two
 553:   training seeds; it does not establish permutation invariance.
